items.caption:
REM nappers did better on word puzzles.
In a 2009 UC San Diego study of 77 people, those whose nap included REM sleep improved by almost 40% on word-association puzzles linked to the morning's. Quiet rest and non-REM sleep brought no improvement. A lab puzzle, not proof for everyday creativity.

items.caption:
Dreams may be your mind wandering, asleep.
A 2013 review compared reports of dreaming and mind wandering and found both are emotional, loosely narrated, tied to current concerns and memory, with little awareness of one's own thoughts. A hypothesis from a review, not a proven fact.

items.caption:
Elephant seals nap while sinking.
Brain sensors on wild seals showed short naps on deep dives, and movement data from many tagged seals put their sleep at about 2 hours a day at sea on average, vs about 10 hours a day on land (Science, 2023). In REM sleep some turned upside down as they drifted down. One idea from the researchers: deep water may be safer from predators.
